Subject: Follow-up: caching & pricing assumptions for Acme pilot

Hi Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our call: 

Recap
- Initial expected volumes: 8-12M tokens / month for first 3 months, ramping to ~40-60M tokens / month in Q3 if onboarding goes well.
- Primary workload: product Q&A + personalization snippets; prompts are fairly consistent across sessions with a handful of dynamic user tokens.
- Target budget: you said a preferred effective spend in the $15-$25 per 1M tokens range for the pilot.

Pricing & caching assumptions (high level)
- List price (example): $25 / 1M tokens (Redwood hosted API list example)
- Effective price with caching = list_price * (1 - cache_hit_rate)
  - e.g., 40% hit rate -> effective = $25 * (1 - 0.4) = $15 / 1M tokens
- Hit rate sensitivity: 20% -> $20 / 1M; 60% -> $10 / 1M (same list price)

Caching approach we discussed
- Prefix/prompt caching: static system prompts & few-shot examples cached across requests.
- Session KV caching: persistent KV cache for a session reduces recomputation for repeated tokens (useful for multi-turn).
- Short-term prefix cache vs longer-lived shared prefix cache: shared prefixes across users (e.g., product description) drive higher hit rates.

Open items / next steps
1) Marcus will share a short doc with hit-rate scenarios and example effective unit-cost calculations (attached spreadsheet).
2) Sam - please confirm the 8-12M starting volume and whether personalization increases per-request prompt variance (this will materially affect hit rate).
3) If budget target looks good, we’ll send a 30-day pilot SOW + DocuSign link and provision a dedicated pilot environment to measure real hit rate from logs.

I attached a short spreadsheet with example hit-rate scenarios and a draft SOW for the pilot.

Thanks - Marissa

Subject: Re: Follow-up: caching & pricing assumptions for Acme pilot - hit rate details

Hi Sam - quick technical notes on hit-rate modeling and impact on effective pricing. Posting the short math here so it’s easy to follow, and I’ve put full scenarios in the attached spreadsheet.

Key assumptions to estimate cache hit rate
- Shared prefix fraction (f_shared): portion of tokens that are identical across requests (system prompts, product descriptions, canonical few-shot examples).
- Variable personalization fraction (f_personal): tokens that vary per-user/session (user name, recent actions).
- Generated vs prompt tokens: cache only benefits prompt tokens (the model still needs to run generate tokens). If a request is 200 prompt tokens + 800 generated tokens, caching helps on the 200 prompt tokens portion.

Simple effective-cost formula (per 1M total tokens billed under list pricing):
- Let list_price = P ($/1M tokens)
- Let hit_rate = H (0-1) measured on prompt-token volume fraction
- effective_price ≈ P * (1 - H)  (when H is measured against billable prompt tokens fraction)

Worked example (illustrative)
- P = $25 / 1M tokens
- Request breakdown avg: 200 prompt tokens (cacheable) + 800 generated tokens (non-cacheable) -> prompt fraction = 200/1000 = 20%
- If cache hits cover 50% of prompt tokens, overall billable reduction = H_total = 0.5 * prompt_fraction = 0.5 * 0.2 = 0.1 -> 10% overall token reduction
- Effective price per 1M total tokens = P * (1 - 0.1) = $25 * 0.9 = $22.50 / 1M tokens

Note on metrics to measure in pilot
- Measure cache hit rate both on prompt-token basis and request-basis (full-request reuse).
- Track effective tokens billed vs raw token usage to compute real-world effective $/1M.
- Look for high shared prefix reuse (e.g., help center responses, static product copy) - these are the biggest lever for cheaper unit economics.

Practical guidance
- If your personalization is small (~50-100 tokens) and most of the prompt is shared, expect 30-50% prompt-level hit rates for typical e-commerce Q&A templates.
- If personalization dominates (>50% of prompt), hit rates will be correspondingly lower and effective price improvement will be limited.

I’ll upload a sampling script and a short benchmark notebook after the pilot kick-off so we can measure real hit rates from logs.

- Marcus

Sam - thanks for the quick reply and for the personalization detail. Next steps to get the pilot moving: 

1) Please confirm final starting volume (we’ll use 10M tokens/mo as a working assumption unless you want to adjust).
2) Confirm target effective price - you mentioned ~$20 / 1M as the preferred target. If we assume list price $25, that implies needing ~20% overall token reduction (via cache + other optimizations) to hit $20 effective. Marcus’ note above shows how prompt fraction interacts with that goal.
3) Sign SOW / pilot - I’ve attached the draft SOW and pricing scenarios. I’ll send a DocuSign link for approval once you confirm the volumes/target.
4) Pilot measurement plan: 14-day measurement window after provisioning, we’ll share a short sampling script to measure prompt vs generated token fractions and compute observed hit rate.

If that sounds good I’ll send the DocuSign link and schedule a 30-minute pilot kickoff with Marcus and your engineering lead (Jordan). Proposed kickoff: Monday 2027-04-26 10:00am PT.

Thanks - looking forward to it.

Marissa
